en: Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Abu Usama narrated to us: Hisham informed us, from his father, from Aisha regarding His saying: {And they request from you a legal ruling concerning women. Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning them} (Quran 4:127) the verse. She said: It refers to the female orphan who is in the care of a man, and perhaps she shares in his property, even in a palm tree, so he desires—meaning to marry her—and dislikes marrying her to another man lest he become a partner in his property, and so he prevents her from marrying.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shayba narrated to us: Abda ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Hisham, from his father, from Aisha regarding His saying: {and what is recited to you in the Book concerning orphan girls to whom you do not give what has been decreed for them while you desire to marry them} (Quran 4:127). She said: It was revealed concerning the orphan girl who is in the care of a man and shares in his property, and he is disinclined to marry her himself, yet dislikes marrying her to someone else lest that person become a partner in his property, so he prevents her from marrying; he neither marries her himself nor gives her in marriage to another.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shayba and Abu Kurayb both narrated to us, saying: Abu Usama narrated to us: Hisham narrated to us, from his father, from Aisha regarding His saying: {And if you fear that you will not deal justly with the orphan girls} (Quran 4:3). She said: It was revealed concerning a man who has under his guardianship an orphan girl whose guardian and heir he is, and she possesses wealth while she has no one to advocate on her behalf; so he does not marry her off because of her wealth, harming her and treating her companionship poorly. Thus He said: {if you fear that you will not deal justly with the orphan girls, then marry those that please you of women} (Quran 4:3), meaning: whatever I have made lawful for you, and leave this one whom you harm.

Al-Hasan al-Hulwani and Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us, both from Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa'd: my father narrated to us, from Salih, from Ibn Shihab: Urwah informed me that he asked Aisha about the saying of Allah: {And if you fear that you will not deal justly with the orphan girls}, and he related the hadith similar to the hadith of Yunus from az-Zuhri, adding at its end: 'because of their disinclination toward them when they possess little wealth and beauty.'

Abu al-Tahir Ahmad ibn Amr ibn Sarh and Harmalah ibn Yahya at-Tujibi narrated to me—Abu al-Tahir said: narrated to us, while Harmalah said: informed us—Ibn Wahb: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab: Urwah ibn al-Zubayr informed me that he asked Aisha about the saying of Allah: {And if you fear that you will not deal justly with the orphan girls, then marry those that please you of women, two or three or four}. She said: O son of my sister, this refers to an orphan girl who is in the custody of her guardian and shares in his wealth, and her wealth and beauty attract him, so her guardian wishes to marry her without being equitable regarding her dowry by giving her what another man would give her. Thus, they were forbidden from marrying them unless they treated them justly and gave them the highest customary dowry appropriate for them, and they were commanded to marry women other than them who pleased them. Urwah said: Aisha said: Then the people later sought a ruling from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) concerning them, and so Allah, the Mighty and Sublime, revealed: {And they request from you a legal ruling concerning women. Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning them and what is recited to you in the Book concerning orphan girls to whom you do not give what has been decreed for them while you desire to marry them} (Quran 4:127). She said: And what Allah Most High mentioned as being recited to you in the Book is the first verse in which Allah said: {And if you fear that you will not deal justly with the orphan girls, then marry those that please you of women}. Aisha said: And the saying of Allah in the other verse: {while you desire to marry them} refers to the disinclination of one of you from the orphan girl in his custody when she possesses little wealth and beauty. Therefore, they were forbidden from marrying those among orphan women whose wealth and beauty they desired except with justice, on account of their disinclination toward them.

Abd ibn Humayd narrated to me: Ja'far ibn Awn informed us: Abu Umays informed us, from Qays ibn Muslim, from Tariq ibn Shihab, who said: A man from the Jews came to Umar and said: 'O Commander of the Believers, there is a verse in your Book which you recite; had it been revealed to us, the company of Jews, we would have taken that day as a day of celebration (eid).' He said: 'And which verse is it?' He said: {This day I have perfected for you your religion and completed My favor upon you and have approved for you Islam as your religion} (Quran 5:3). Umar said: 'I indeed know the day on which it was revealed and the place where it was revealed; it was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) at Arafat on a Friday.'

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shayba and Abu Kurayb narrated to us—and the wording is that of Abu Bakr—he said: Abdullah ibn Idris narrated to us, from his father, from Qays ibn Muslim, from Tariq ibn Shihab, who said: The Jews said to Umar: 'Had this verse: {This day I have perfected for you your religion and completed My favor upon you and have approved for you Islam as your religion} (Quran 5:3) been revealed to us, the company of Jews, knowing the day on which it was revealed, we would have taken that day as a celebration (eid).' Umar said: 'I indeed know the day on which it was revealed, the hour, and where the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) was when it was revealed; it was revealed on the night of Jam' (Muzdalifah), while we were with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) at Arafat.'

Abu Khaythama Zuhayr ibn Harb and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me—and the wording is that of Ibn al-Muthanna—both said: Abd al-Rahman—and he is Ibn Mahdi—narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from Qays ibn Muslim, from Tariq ibn Shihab, that the Jews said to Umar: 'You recite a verse which, had it been revealed among us, we would have taken that day as a celebration (eid).' Umar said: 'I indeed know where it was revealed, which day it was revealed, and where the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) was when it was revealed; it was revealed at Arafah while the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) was standing at Arafah.' Sufyan said: I doubt whether it was on a Friday or not—meaning: {This day I have perfected for you your religion and completed My favor upon you} (Quran 5:3).

Amr ibn Muhammad ibn Bukayr an-Naqid, al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Hulwani, and Abd ibn Humayd narrated to me—Abd said: narrated to me, while the other two said: narrated to us—Ya'qub—meaning Ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa'd: my father narrated to us, from Salih—and he is Ibn Kaysan—from Ibn Shihab, who said: Anas ibn Malik informed me that Allah, the Mighty and Sublime, sent revelation successively to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) before his death until he passed away, and the revelation was most abundant on the day the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) passed away.

Muhammad ibn Rafi narrated to us: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Ma'mar narrated to us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: This is what Abu Hurayrah narrated to us from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him). He mentioned several hadiths, and among them: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: It was said to the Children of Israel: {Enter the gate prostrating and say: 'Relieve us,' so that your sins will be forgiven you}, but they altered it, and entered the gate dragging themselves on their buttocks, and they said: 'A grain in a hair.'
